_comment: The MPL TestServer Configuration_Set: exactly one `product`, exactly one
feature catalog (`features`), and one Configuration_Entry per
Language_Server (Requirements 7.1, 7.2).
TWO DIVERGENCES from the ESDK TestServer's Configuration_Set, both direct
consequences of the MPL living in a single repository:
1. No per-entry `libraryRepository`. The ESDK schema carries library
coordinates per entry because each language's ESDK lives in its own
repository. The MPL's Artifact_Under_Test is ALWAYS this repository's
Dafny source, transpiled from the working tree. Recording coordinates
for it would record a constant, and imply -- falsely -- that the
library could come from somewhere else (Requirement 7.4).
2. The Feature_Declaration (`supportedFeatures` / `unsupportedFeatures`)
is inline in the entry. In the ESDK, a language that owns a repository
declares its features there; no MPL language owns a repository, so
every declaration lives here (Requirement 7.5).
`majorVersion` is retained even with a single language because a server's
identity is the (language, majorVersion) tuple: when the MPL ships a 2.x,
`java-v1` and `java-v2` must be separately nameable (Requirement 7.7). It
tracks the major of `javaMPLVersion` in ../../project.properties.
`serverLocation.path` is relative to the repository root.
